title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is studying the boundary of the Deligne–Mumford compactification of M_{g,ν} through its 'MD-graphes', i.e. stable dual graphs. Each vertex α carries a genus g_α, a number ν_α of marked points, and a valence μ̃_α (number of half-edges, so a loop counts twice). The closed stratum attached to G has normalization (up to a finite group, the 'groupe modulaire' Γ of the previous page) equal to ∏_α M_{g_α, ν_α+μ̃_α}. Its dimension, the 'dimension modulaire', is therefore

(67) δ(G) = Σ_α δ_α, with δ_α = 3(g_α−1) + ν_α + μ̃_α.

Stability forces each δ_α ≥ 0, so δ(G) ∈ {1,2} leaves only two possibilities: one or two of the δ_α equal 1 and the rest vanish, or a single δ_α equals 2 and the rest vanish. The previous page treated δ(G) = 0, i.e. 0-dimensional strata, which are trivalent genus-0 graphs; it listed their groups Γ and Γ^! for ambient dimension ≤ 2.

Case II, δ(G) = 1, is classified as follows. There is a unique vertex α0 with δ_{α0} = 1. This happens in exactly one of two ways:
- g_{α0} = 1 and total weight ν+μ̃ = 1, so α0 is a genus-1 tail, or an isolated genus-1 vertex with one marked point;
- g_{α0} = 0 and total weight 4, with (ν, μ̃) ∈ {(4,0), (3,1), (2,2), (1,3), (0,4)}.

Every other vertex α has δ_α = 0. Since stability excludes the case g = 1, n = 0, such a vertex has genus 0, valence μ̃_α ≤ 3 and ν_α = 3 − μ̃_α.

The next page concludes that the normalized stratum is canonically M_{0,4} or M_{1,1}, possibly up to a finite group. It also lists the elementary cases: M_{0,4} with Γ = S_4, and M_{1,1}.

Purpose: this is the systematic enumeration of the 1-dimensional (and next, 2-dimensional) boundary strata. These are the building blocks of the 'Lego' of the Teichmüller tower in modular dimension ≤ 2 described in the Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: No mathematical errors. The case analysis is correct and complete given stability: δ_α ≥ 0 for every stable vertex, and δ_α = 0 forces (g, n) = (0, 3) because (1, 0) is unstable.
Minor notational looseness: the underbrace labels the summand δ_α while the bracket is drawn around the whole sum.

ideas.what: Dimension of a boundary stratum of M̄_{g,ν} as a sum over vertices of 3g_α−3+n_α, with n_α = marked points plus valence
ideas.modern_name: dimension of the stratum M_Γ for a stable graph Γ
ideas.where_published: Implicit in Esquisse d'un programme (modular dimension of strata)

ideas.what: Classification of 1-dimensional boundary strata: one vertex of type (0,4) or (1,1), all others trivalent genus 0
ideas.modern_name: F-curves / one-dimensional boundary strata (1-skeleton of the stratification)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses strata of modular dimension ≤ 2 and the elementary pieces M_{0,4} and M_{1,1}, without this explicit enumeration

ideas.what: Reduction of the dimension 1 and 2 cases to distributions of the δ_α (one or two equal to 1, or one equal to 2)
ideas.modern_name: low-dimensional strata used in the two-level principle (Lego of the Teichmüller tower)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §§ on the Teichmüller tower

missed.claim: This is an explicit, early (pre-1984?) classification of the one-dimensional boundary strata of M̄_{g,ν}. It is exactly the description later called F-curves: a (0,4) or (1,1) vertex with all other vertices trivalent genus 0. It is not new mathematics, but it documents Grothendieck's independent and systematic use of these strata, with their automorphism groups, as building blocks.
missed.quote: les sommets α ≠ α0 sont de genre 0, d'ordre μ̃_α ≤ 3, et pour un tel α le poids ν_α est égal à 3 − μ̃_α
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority and context only: it links the Esquisse 'Lego' programme with the F-curve stratification used in the birational geometry of M̄_{g,n}. The connection is already known in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: A correct, routine enumeration of 1-dimensional stable-graph strata, the standard F-curve description. It is interesting as documentation of the Esquisse programme, but contains nothing unknown to specialists.
transcription_corrections: In (68) the word 'point' before 'isolé' is struck out; the reading should be '…ou isolé de poids marqué 1)'.
In (69) a struck-out word 'tel que' (or 'tel quel') precedes 'ν_α est égal à 3 − μ̃_α'; the word 'marqué' is not clearly what is struck.
Line 2 reads 'G de dimension modulaire' followed by a mark, possibly 'est' or an arrow, before formula (67); the transcription's 'δ(G)' there is an interpolation.
